0ef306e13a591f3124f89708c938c9286157534a.caption: A "Drawer" component marked as a "Don't" example. It includes a topline with the text "Hallo!" and "Maxime Doe," and a small ghost button with an "X" icon. The example is incorrect because the topline does not clearly convey the drawer's purpose, as it uses informal language and a name instead of a specific page, feature title, or object.

243693fd94c2482ef235b69fe1b0216ae170ce06.caption: A Drawer component with a header area, a content area, and a footer area. The header area, labeled as "Heading," is marked by callout 1. The content area, marked by callout 2, contains a placeholder component with the text "❖ Placeholder - Replace this content," and can be replaced with custom content. The footer area, marked by callout 3, includes three buttons: a "Primary CTA" button with a filled variant, a "Secondary CTA" button with an outline variant, and a "Tertiary CTA" button also with an outline variant. All buttons are enabled and of medium size.

2ceba57e752074bb6f7e11ba5039140923a6038e.caption: A Drawer component with custom areas, showing the layout of a header, content, and footer within the drawer, along with a backdrop. The numbered callouts point to the following areas: 1 is the Custom header area, 2 is the Custom content area, 3 is the Custom footer area, and 4 is the Backdrop. The header and footer areas are optional, while the content area is mandatory.

307d1f56a147c51602a2ca8e225769f77a0e7be7.caption: A Drawer component with backdrop dimming. The backdrop fades from 0 to 100% opacity with a black color at 50% intensity over 400 milliseconds using motion-functional-ease-out easing. The layout includes a heading, a placeholder area, and three buttons labeled Primary CTA, Secondary CTA, and Tertiary CTA, each with specified variants and states. The Drawer moves from either the left or right, and the backdrop fades in as described.

393a1618d3f27cd30d093baca926a328a0147e0c.caption: A header-drawer component variant for desktop viewports, styled with a heading. It includes a heading text labeled "Heading," a back button on the left, and a close button on the right. The text next to the figure specifies that the close icon on the right is preferred regardless of the drawer's placement.

4e893babfa56a2f257ad92821008184619c65355.caption: Two variants of a Drawer component, illustrating the optional footer area. Callout 1 points to a Drawer with only a close icon and no footer area, indicating that in some cases a close icon is sufficient. Callout 2 points to a Drawer with a short content area and a button placed closer to the content, demonstrating that when the content is very short, the button can be positioned nearer to it.

504f6d630af9db6877838b713c13d11c2f61ca72.caption: Various variants and elements of the header-drawer and footer-drawer components for both desktop and mobile viewports. Each variant shows different combinations of elements such as heading, back button, subline, and close button for the header-drawer, and button arrangements for the footer-drawer. The figure illustrates different layouts and states, including horizontal and vertical directions and primary positions for buttons in the footer-drawer.

70326ed742be0c8e0deac79704ac77d9d991936a.caption: A Drawer component with three levels of navigation, labeled "Level 1," "Level 2," and "Level 3," all within the same container. The example illustrates a consistent width across different levels of the drawer, aiming to reduce user distraction by minimizing transitions. This layout is marked as a "Do" example because it maintains a uniform width, enhancing user experience by showing deeper navigation levels within the same drawer container.

7120ab19394cb82fe35f2e97f41952beb942f8f4.caption: A "Don't" example for using drawers in a UI design system, specifically the STIHL Design System. It shows a layout with a drawer open, containing a list of navigation items such as "STIHL Infos," "Kontaktformular," "Impressum," "Rechtliche Unterlagen," "App-Informationen," "App-Version," and "Verwendete Bibliotheken." The example is marked as incorrect because it demonstrates opening multiple layers on top of each other, which is not recommended. A small button labeled "Don't" with a red background and white text is visible, indicating the incorrect usage. The drawer includes detailed text under the heading "IMpressum," providing information such as the service provider details...

732ae57bc556870b98a9ea32ce88772a99717eec.caption: A drawer component used for secondary actions, such as showing additional information. It includes a header with the title "Technical details" and a close button, followed by a list of technical specifications. Each specification is a link in the default variant, highlighted and enabled, without an icon. The measurements provided are: Rated Voltage is 36 V, Weight is 3.1 kg, Sound Pressure Level is 77 dB(A), Sound Power Level is 91 dB(A), Vibration Value Left/Right is 3.7/2 m/s², Total Length is 168 cm, Cutting Circle Diameter is 350 mm, Battery Runtime with AK 10 is up to 13 min, Battery Runtime with AK 20 is up to 30 min, Battery Runtime with AK 30 is up to 38 min...

74c00f8747237336eae0871c7040b7d2ef3a2ff1.caption: The use of multiple drawers in a UI design system, specifically the STIHL Design System. It shows three mobile screens, each depicting different states of drawer interactions. The first screen shows a closed state with no drawers open. The second screen shows two drawers labeled "Menu" and "Filter" that can be triggered from the same side. The third screen shows a single drawer open from the opposite side. The figure demonstrates that drawers can slide in from the same side for connected tasks or from different sides for distinct task-flows, and notes that multiple drawers are never opened simultaneously.

7569759a93c2a60a4f7d964d64d3f847dab77d12.caption: A Drawer component in its open state, with a focus indicator on the first actionable element. The focus indicator is a blue circle with a white "i" inside, pointing to a black bar, which represents the first actionable element within the drawer. Numbered callout 1 points to this focus indicator, illustrating the focus management when the drawer opens.

79514cb00e1f9269617a92ebe4024d377e3ac5fe.caption: A "Don't" example of a drawer component in a UI design system. It shows a full-screen drawer, which is marked as incorrect because the drawer component cannot be full-screen. The measurements labeled 100% refer to the width and height of the screen, indicating that the drawer occupies the entire screen area, which is not recommended.

7a733249e1b5abe4d512d1c84a54596a4f8124af.caption: A header-drawer component in the desktop viewport, displaying technical details with various specifications such as Rated Voltage, Weight, Sound Pressure Level, and others. The numbered callout 1 points to a close button in the header-drawer, which triggers an exit animation when clicked. The numbered callout 2 points to a dimmed backdrop, which can be clicked to close the drawer, although this feature can be disabled. The technical details include measurements like 36 V for Rated Voltage, 3.1 kg for Weight, 77 dB(A) for Sound Pressure Level, and so on.

7f7418451a0f29bf25a0d0b83d8cf682ffbdf766.caption: A Drawer component with backdrop dimming, showing the drawer moving out to the left or right. The backdrop has a fade animation from 100% to 0% opacity with a black color at 50% intensity, lasting 400ms with motion-functional-ease-in easing. The layout includes a heading at the top, a placeholder area in the center, and three buttons at the bottom labeled Primary CTA, Secondary CTA, and Tertiary CTA, each with different variants and states. The Primary CTA button is filled, while the Secondary and Tertiary CTA buttons are outlined.

87d91dd1b292b1753ee5b189c07c9650a4009caa.caption: The layout and width constraints of a drawer component in a UI design system. The maximum width of the drawer is 1730px, adjusting to the width of the inserted content without exceeding this size. The minimum space between the browser edge and the drawer is 80px on bigger screens and 32px on smaller screens.

8a7ae9bb80e2cb8525f470927bf9c030bd1e88ab.caption: A formatting warning for a drawer component in a UI design system. It shows a "Don't" example with a full sentence in the header area: "Are you sure you want to add the “speech to Text” service to the node-test-app?" The layout includes a highlighted button labeled "Don't" and a ghost button with an "x" icon for closing. There are also examples of primary, secondary, and tertiary call-to-action buttons, each with the variant filled, outline, and outline respectively, all in an enabled state and medium size. The text next to the figure advises not to write full sentences in the header area.

8f26cc21898424a526ca72155fee81efab0e2546.caption: Two variants of a Drawer component, illustrating different button placements based on the side from which the drawer appears. The left example shows a drawer opening from the right with a close button positioned at the top right corner and a secondary button at the bottom left. The right example shows a drawer opening from the left with a close button at the top right corner and a secondary button at the bottom right. The dashed purple lines indicate the boundaries of the drawer components.

9e1bb4c544c0cfd49c06a8dcfef3a3753cbce82a.caption: A drawer component with a header-drawer containing a heading, a close button, and text. The header-drawer is followed by a placeholder with text and an image, and a footer-dialog with two buttons labeled "Close" and "Cancel" arranged horizontally, with the "Close" button in the primary position on the left. The text "You will read this first" is at the top, followed by "And then you will read this line next." The layout is for a desktop viewport.

9f0deda56b04bc1f20b46ce4dca5ceaabe2aaca0.caption: The Drawer component in the STIHL Design System, displaying its variants and states for desktop and mobile viewports. It shows the Drawer with different placements (left and right), viewports (Desktop and Mobile), and overflow states (false and true). The Drawer includes a header-drawer with a heading, back button, close button, and a footer-drawer with buttons arranged horizontally on desktop and vertically on mobile. The width of the Drawer adjusts to the content, while the height is always 100%. The header area and footer area are sticky, allowing the content area to scroll if there is overflow...

a02fe7a3b5ab860416621e5420af06e4bb5bd8e3.caption: The content overflow behavior of a drawer component in both desktop and mobile viewports. The header and footer areas are fixed and sticky, with an outline appearing at the bottom and top respectively when content overflows, making the content scrollable. The desktop variant shows a horizontal footer-dialog with three buttons, while the mobile variant displays a vertical footer-dialog with the same buttons. The header-drawer includes a heading, back button, and close button in both viewports.

a59548d39843f062967400d9e010d300d1331e9c.caption: A Stepper navigation component in a Drawer, showing a multi-step process with three visible steps and a restart action within the content area. The stepper includes visual indicators for progress, with the second step highlighted in orange, indicating it is the current step. The header area of the drawer is left empty, and the drawer is positioned to slide in from the right side. The steps are labeled as STEP LABEL with descriptive text underneath each label. The close button is located at the bottom of the drawer.

ae41708a490eb20cfc80d050b7f98e5893c64bff.caption: A Drawer component with different action positions and their relatedness to the drawer's sliding direction. The measurements indicate the width of the drawer and the position of the action button. The first and fourth drawers slide from the right with the action button at the bottom right, while the second and third drawers slide from the left with the action button at the top left. This layout demonstrates how the position of the action influences the intuitive direction from which the drawer slides.

af4bdf2e7d843157a0405cc8a060ff14429b3f62.caption: The layout and styling of a Drawer component in a UI design system, comparing desktop and mobile views. It displays various Button components with different variants such as highlight, ghost, filled, and outline, along with states like enabled, sizes like small and medium, and icon positions. The layout examples show the positioning of buttons in both horizontal and vertical directions, with primary positions on the left and right for both desktop and mobile views.

b5f1b79ce66505c4519dae314f47efaf349192c9.caption: The minimum width requirement for a Drawer component in a UI design system. The measurement of 272 pixels refers to the minimum width to which the drawer can adjust based on the smallest viewport size. The figure shows two variants of the Drawer component, one in a larger and one in a smaller viewport, both demonstrating the minimum width constraint.

c20f06b31b499842b5df1cf63ae252dc3e5a0404.caption: A Drawer component with short content, illustrating the layout for when the custom content area is half filled. The button is placed close to the content, and the footer area is left empty as specified. The component includes a close button at the top right corner and a horizontal bar within the content area.

c55ef27df5daa6cb155f2d95204c8fa967cae173.caption: Three formatting examples for headers within a drawer component. The first callout points to a combination of a "Topline" and "Heading L" with a back button. The second callout shows "Heading L Uppercase" combined with a back button. The third callout highlights a "Title component" suitable for impactful and emotional headers. Each example includes a small ghost variant back button on the left side and a close button on the right side.

c81838d8a95c949d5a5e26f30444595864f23c00.caption: A Drawer component with different Close icon placements. Callout 1 points to drawers with the Close icon on the right, which is the preferred placement for both left and right drawers. Callout 2 points to drawers with the Close icon on the left, which is not ideal but acceptable.

d9e646ba233ddc4abbb3f589fb08eeafc3ca3f54.caption: A "header-drawer" with a heading "New active time" and a back button, along with a close button at the top right. It includes a form with fields for "Active Time", "Start Time", "End Time", and "Mowing Zone", with options like "Enable instance" and "Enable series". The "footer-drawer" contains two buttons labeled "Save" and "Cancel". The board is marked as a "Don't" example because the drawer component is not suited for primary tasks such as creating or editing objects, suggesting the use of a new page or dialog component instead.

dbeadcdc053f2739175f19080a36b09c09c08eb2.caption: A Drawer component in two states, demonstrating how its width adjusts dynamically based on the content displayed. The first state shows "Content 1" within the drawer, and the second state shows "Content 2," indicating that the drawer's width changes to fit the content when it is opened. The text "content in drawer changes" highlights this dynamic behavior.

dd0e24dc2aad2bcd21c6bb503a161412d01ac005.caption: A Drawer component that spans the full height of the screen in two different width variants. Each measurement labeled 100% indicates that the height of the drawer covers the entire height of the screen. The component includes a close button at the top right corner and a bar at the bottom, with the main content area in between.
